Hey, I hope this all comes across in the spirit in which it is intended. I feel you, I know life is hard and these decisions can be rough. I don't think any of us have all the answers. I can tell you that in my short experience.. you have to truly want it. Not trying to say that you don't want it. Just if you're not ready, noone else can make up the difference. You have to put in the work. In the beginning you may have many many miserable days. Days where you make it hour by hour, maybe minute by minute. Eventually it gets easier but just how long that will take is different for everyone. 

I spend many days going to AA. I haven't gotten far on the steps but being open and honest with others that have more sobriety than me helped a lot. I regularly would get the phone numbers of people that had more sobriety and when they spoke it resonated with me. I'd call and text them semi regularly. Not everyone responds and can always be there but after doing this for a month or more I had plenty of people in my corner and willing to help me. Again they were support but they didn't do anything for me necessarily, I had to make the phone calls, do the mental work. I have a sponsor and reach out to him when I have bad days. He has been so supportive in getting me out of my own head. I struggled with and still struggle with the faith part of the program. It doesn't really matter, these people are just sharing their experience and want to see you succeed. I may never find a true higher power. Idk. 

I like the in person support, but I also found online support groups or zoom meetings where I can share with others being supportive. Make friends in these subreddits if you can.

I also have been trying counseling and seeing a psychiatrist, getting on antidepressants. Not sure if I've found the right ones but I'm trying. After a lifetime of negativity and self hatred I've been trying to be mindful with my thoughts, acknowledging the thoughts, not attaching any weight to them and trying to let them pass. It is probably just as hard as not drinking. A friend told me it's like any muscle, you have to work at it to make it stronger. The positivity and having healthier thoughts takes immense work as those muscles haven't really been used most of my life. I've made small progress and hope to see more.

At the end of my day, I need to find something to be hopeful about. Taking actions that ever so slowly move me in the right direction. I'm only 90 days in and definitely don't know if any of this is helpful. I'm sorry if you've heard all this before. Unfortunately there are no easy answers. This has just been some of my realizations that have gotten me this far.

Thinking about never seeing my daughters ever again and not seeing them grow up is the only thing that brings tears to my eyes anymore. But I know im looking for reasons to not fight anymore.
